headline: Fuel markets retreat as Middle East diplomacy offsets tight supply
intro: Crude and diesel pulled back as traders bet on a US-brokered Iran de-escalation, but with ULSD still near $4.69 and refining margins near record highs, nobody's calling this a trend yet.
overview: Oil and diesel futures eased on hopes for Middle East diplomacy even as crude inventories fell to a three-month low and Saudi export disruption headlines kept a floor under prices. Refiners posted blockbuster Q3 results on record refining margins — Shell, Phillips 66, Valero, and TotalEnergies all beat expectations — while PBF pushed efficiency gains to capture more of the current margin environment. On policy, Canada's proposed Clean Fuel Regulations changes and US RFS/E15 reform efforts continue to shape the biofuels and SAF landscape, alongside a fresh SAF offtake deal for Singapore Airlines.

stories.title: Markets Weigh Middle East Diplomacy Against Persistent Fuel Tightness
stories.summary: Energy markets saw broad selling as hopes for a new Middle East peace agreement pushed prices lower to start the day.

stories.title: Nymex Overview: Oil, Diesel Retreat as U.S. Steps Up Diplomacy -- OPIS
stories.summary: Crude and diesel contracts fell sharply as US diplomatic efforts to engage Iranian hard-liners eased fears of war escalation, per OPIS.

stories.title: Oil Eases as Europe Readies First Emergency Diesel Batch
stories.summary: Oil prices eased as traders assessed a diplomatic push for a temporary US-Iran peace deal, with Europe readying its first emergency diesel batch.

stories.title: WTI Back Above $100 on Saudi Attack, U.S. Inventory Draws
stories.summary: WTI climbed back above $100 after EIA reported commercial crude inventories fell 1.9 million bbl to 410.6 million bbl, the lowest since July 31.

stories.title: EIA: US crude oil inventories down 1.9 million bbl
stories.summary: US crude oil inventories fell 1.9 million bbl to 410.6 million bbl, now 4% below the five-year average, per EIA.

stories.title: Saudi Refinery Claim Lifts Oil Near US$115
stories.summary: Houthi claims of a strike on a Saudi refinery lifted Brent near $115 on Oct. 28, with US gasoline averaging $4.27/gal.

stories.title: Oil Rises with Iran Attack Report, Israeli Election in Focus
stories.summary: Oil rose as traders weighed the possibility of renewed US/Israel strikes on Iran following an attack report.

stories.title: Shell's third-quarter earnings rise on record refining margins, stronger gas results
stories.summary: Shell's Q3 earnings rose on record refining margins and stronger gas results despite continued Middle East supply disruptions.

stories.title: Shell Approves $5B Buyback as Refining Boosts Profit
stories.summary: Shell approved a $5B buyback as record refining margins, driven by the Iran war and Russia-Ukraine conflict, boosted profits.

stories.title: Phillips 66 Delivers Profit above Expectations
stories.summary: Phillips 66 reported $5.62 billion in Q3 net profit, up from $3.85 billion the prior quarter, on higher refining margins.

stories.title: Valero Energy stock: Buyback capacity expands after strong quarter
stories.summary: Valero reported $46.1 billion in Q3 revenue and $6.83 billion net income, expanding buyback capacity after a strong quarter.

stories.title: PBF Energy boosts refinery improvement efforts, targets > $350 MM in savings
stories.summary: PBF Energy identified small- to mid-scale projects targeting over $350 million in savings by improving refinery utilization and yields.

stories.title: Texas House Members Push RFS Reforms as Senate Farm Bill Would Advance Year-Round E15
stories.summary: 22 House Republicans led by Texas lawmakers urged pairing year-round E15 approval with RFS reforms in the farm bill.

stories.title: Singapore Ailines to offtake next-generation Sustainable Aviation Fuel from Aether Fuels
stories.summary: Singapore Airlines signed an agreement to purchase up to 4,800 tonnes of next-generation SAF from Aether Fuels over three years.

decks.analysis:
## PBF Energy Q3 2026 — Refined Fuels Markets Takeaways

- **Throughput & margin capture surged on stronger crack spreads**: Total crude/feedstock throughput was 923.8 Mbpd (vs. 871.0 Mbpd Q3 2025), with consolidated gross margin of $25.54/bbl (vs. $0.49/bbl) and gross refining margin ex-special items of $34.56/bbl (vs. $9.00/bbl). Benchmark cracks nearly tripled y/y: Dated Brent (NYH) 2-1-1 at $64.77 (vs. $25.82), LLS (Gulf Coast) 2-1-1 at $69.06 (vs. $24.41), ANS (West Coast-SF) 3-2-1 at $73.33 (vs. $30.59) — indicating PBF captured a larger share of a much wider crack environment, especially on the West Coast where Martinez's return to full ops (May 2026) drove margin per barrel to $25.55 (vs. -$7.78 loss in Q3 2025).

- **Martinez fully back online, insurance claim nearing close**: Refinery returned to full operations in May 2026; cumulative insurance proceeds received to date total $1.25 billion, with the claim process expected to finalize before year-end 2026. Residual exposure capped by a $30 million deductible/retention.

- **Turnaround schedule shifted, supporting Q4 supply**: Torrance turnaround completed Q1; Martinez hydrocracker turnaround moved from Q2 to late Q3 (completed with Paulsboro in October); Chalmette and Toledo Q4 turnarounds pushed to 2027 — reducing near-term unplanned downtime risk and supporting Q4 2026 total throughput guidance of 925,000–985,000 bpd (East Coast 300–320K, Mid-Con 155–165K, Gulf Coast 180–190K, West Coast 290–310K). 2026 capex guidance held at $825–875 million (ex-Martinez rebuild).

- **RIN/LCFS exposure rising with RIN prices**: Effective RIN basket price averaged $14.36/bbl in Q3 2026 vs. $6.38/bbl in Q3 2025 — more than doubling, a meaningful cost/benefit swing depending on RVO compliance position; SBR renewable diesel averaged 19,156 bpd in Q3, with Q4 guidance of 18,000–20,000 bpd.

- **Capital allocation favors balance sheet over aggressive capex/buybacks**: Net debt swung to a net cash position (-$425.9 million net debt) after redeeming $500M of 7.875% 2030 notes (via $550M 0% Exchangeable Notes due 2032) and, post-quarter, fully repaying $800M of 9.875% 2030 notes using cash on hand — net debt reduced ~150% vs. Q2 2026. Dividend raised 18% to $0.325/share, signaling confidence in sustained margin capture rather than pivoting to growth capex.

- **RBI cost program scaling**: Run-rate cost improvements from the Refinery Business Improvement initiative expected to grow from over $230 million (2025) to more than $350 million by year-end 2026, a structural tailwind to refining operating expense per barrel ($7.80/bbl in Q3 2026, still up slightly y/y from $7.35/bbl despite higher throughput).

**Signal for fuels markets**: PBF's results reflect a refining margin environment that has structurally re-rated wider across all U.S. coasts (particularly West Coast post-Martinez restart and Gulf/East Coast crack strength), combined with sharply higher RIN costs — a combination that rewards complex, coastal refiners with strong capture rates while reinforcing capital discipline (debt paydown, dividend growth) over capacity expansion.

## Darling Ingredients (DAR) Q3 2026 – Refined Fuels Takeaways

- **DGD throughput & economics inflected sharply**: Q3 2026 production ~315M gallons (vs. 231.5M in Q3-25; Q4 guided to ~325M gallons). DGD Adjusted EBITDA per gallon sold/shipped jumped to **$1.30** from **-$0.02** YoY (YTD: $1.59 vs. $0.13), driven by "robust RVO" and improved margins — though management flags the $0.92/gal 2021–2025 average as the more normalized "mid-cycle" reference (vs. $1.50 up-cycle / $0.33 down-cycle scenarios).

- **Fuel segment EBITDA inflected to +$227.9M** (combined, incl. Darling's 50% DGD share) from $21.6M in Q3-25 (+955%); DGD Adjusted EBITDA (Darling's share) alone was $204.2M vs. -$2.9M prior year, reflecting equity income swing of $165.6M vs. a $45.8M loss a year ago.

- **One-time drags flagged as reversing in Q4**: SAF shipment timing, a short-term hydrogen outage, feedstock lag, and heating-oil price volatility weighed on Q3 Fuel results; management expects these to reverse, supporting a "favorable Q4 outlook" and margins staying strong into 2027.

- **Cash monetization of credits is material**: DAR received $171.0M in cash from DGD in Q3 — $33.4M in dividends plus $137.6M from Production Tax Credit (PTC) sales, underscoring reliance on PTC/blenders' credit monetization alongside RIN economics.
